page: The Microsoft Azure E16-4s_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine configuration within the ESv4 series, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is structured as a constrained-core instance, delivering 128.0 GB of system memory paired with 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon Platinum 8272CL processor clocked at 2.6 GHz. The x86_64 CPU features 35 MB of L3 cache alongside instruction set extensions including AVX-512, VNNI, and AES-NI. The instance includes no bundled local storage and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring remote attached block storage for disk persistence.

Performance profiles reflect the constrained compute allocation alongside high memory capacity. The instance achieves an average single-core Geekbench score of 1225.0 and PassMark memory score of 2364.39, while its uncached read and write memory bandwidths reach 24.02 GB/s and 18.05 GB/s, respectively. Multi-threaded benchmark results, such as a multi-core Geekbench score of 2720.0 and PassMark CPU score of 4439.67, fall into lower percentile brackets due to the four-vCPU ceiling. Redis SET operations reach 3.55 million ops/sec, and static web serving throughput measures 3.94 GB/sec.

This architecture provides a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 32 GB per core, making it cost-efficient for enterprise software setups where licensing is constrained by core count rather than memory volume. The primary tradeoff is moderate multi-core processing throughput alongside the absence of local ephemeral scratch space. The E16-4s_v4 is well tailored for memory-heavy relational databases, large in-memory caches, and enterprise data processing tasks with modest concurrency needs.
